text: DSH Model Hub（DSH 网页插件）：在 Settings 中提供模型配置页，使用 DSH 的 settings、credentials 和 llm RPC。用户可管理模型提供方、模型清单、上下文窗口和 API 密钥，调整 API 错误重试策略，并选择新 Agent 的默认模型。适合需要通过网页端维护 DSH 模型配置的用户；使用所选模型提供方时需配置其 API 密钥。

DSH Model Hub (a DSH web plugin) adds a Settings page for managing model providers, models, context windows, and API keys through DSH RPCs. Users can tune API error retries and select the default model for new Agents. Configure the API key required by the chosen model provider.
想在 DSH 网页设置里添加或修改模型提供方和模型列表。
怎么给不同模型提供方配置 API 密钥和错误重试参数？
How can I choose the default provider and model for new DSH agents?
DSH Model Hub 的功能「提供方与模型管理」：在 Settings 页面编辑提供方资料、模型和上下文窗口，也可添加自定义提供方并保存 API 密钥。
DSH Model Hub 的功能「默认模型与错误重试」：设置 API 错误重试参数，并选择新 Agent 默认使用的提供方与模型。

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · dsh-plugin-model-hub：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/) web plugin that adds a
**Model Hub** settings page for configuring:

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · dsh-plugin-model-hub：- every provider's profile fields (`displayName`, `api`, `baseURL`, `models`) in
  `settings.yaml`,
- per-provider and per-model **context windows** (`defaultContextWindow` on the
  provider, `contextWindow` on each model — the value the web UI shows as the
  context budget, so a 1M-token model displays 1M instead of the 256K pi-ai
  default),
- per-provider **API keys** (stored through the credentials service, never
  written into `settings.yaml`),
- per-provider **API-error retry/backoff tuning** (max retries, initial/max
  wait, jitter, retryable error codes) — the knobs
  [`dsh-llm-retry`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/) executes,
- the **default Agent model**, and
- declaring brand-new pi-ai provider routes (an OpenAI-compatible gateway or any
  protocol `dsh-llm-pi-ai` supports).

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · Why this page exists：The built-in Models settings page reads and writes through the loopback-only
**settings mirror**, which is deliberately unavailable when the GUI is served
over insecure HTTPS or a non-loopback origin ("settings are unavailable in this
browser"). This plugin does **not** depend on that mirror: every read and write
goes straight over the wire through the stock `settings`, `credentials`, and
`llm` RPC domains, so the page works on any origin the harness itself can reach.

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · How it works：- **host half** (`lib/index.js`) — a stub entry that exists so the package is a
  real loader entry in the profile. The web app's client-modules scan only
  discovers client bundles for packages that are active loader entries declaring
  `dsh.client`.
- **client half** (`lib/client.js`) — the browser page and its data layer,
  registered into the `settings.section` slot. It talks to the harness through
  the stock RPC domains; no custom transport is needed.

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · Install：The plugin ships with a bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) that inserts one
loader row, `model-config`. Two equivalent install paths:

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · 1. Via `dsh plugin` (recommended)：From a checkout at `<checkout>`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/path/to/dsh-plugin-model-hub
```

`dsh plugin` runs `pnpm add` in the profile directory, then reconciles the
profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` layer list: any dependency whose manifest
declares `dsh.bundle` (this one does) joins the bundle layers automatically.

For local development, prefer a symlinked spec so source edits take effect
without reinstalling:

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · 1. Via `dsh plugin` (recommended)：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-plugin-model-hub
```

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · 2. Manually：- Add `dsh-plugin-model-hub` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` in
  `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` **and** make it resolvable from the profile
  (e.g. `pnpm --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/web add file:/path/to/dsh-plugin-model-hub`),
  **or**
- merge the row from `cordis.patch.yml` into the profile's
  `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` yourself.

Then restart the profile (`dsh web`) — the client-modules scan runs at
activation, so a fresh boot is required to pick up a new bundle.

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · Using the page：The **Model Config** section appears in Settings (next to the built-in
sections). For each provider row you can:

- see whether a credential is configured,
- edit profile fields and models,
- enter or replace the API key (leaving it blank keeps the stored one),
- override the retry policy — unset fields keep `dsh-llm` defaults
  (normal mode, 5 retries, 500 ms → 10 s exponential backoff, 10% jitter),
- delete a provider whose profile is user-defined (and its stored key).

dsh-plugin-model-hub README · Development：```bash
npm test          # data-layer tests (node:test, no browser needed)
```

The test harness loads `lib/client.js` in a VM with a fake wire api, so the
store, write paths, and retry-policy building are covered without a browser.
